findings.title: All address CRUD uses delivery-boys_show permission — should split show vs mutate
findings.description: DeliveryBoyAddressController applies `permission:delivery-boys_show` to ALL methods: index, store, update, destroy, show (line 22). This is inconsistent with DeliveryBoyController which correctly splits permissions: _show, _create, _edit, _delete. A user with READ permission to a delivery boy can therefore CREATE/UPDATE/DELETE their addresses. RBAC discipline violation.
findings.reproduction: Read DeliveryBoyAddressController.php line 22 + compare DeliveryBoyController.php line 29-33.
findings.recommendation: Split permissions per HTTP verb: index/show → _show ; store → _create ; update → _edit ; destroy → _delete. Mirrors DeliveryBoyController convention.

findings.title: Frontend show() relies entirely on OrderService for authz — boundary check defensive
findings.description: Frontend DeliveryBoyOrderController::show calls OrderService::deliveryBoyOrderDetails which DOES enforce delivery_boy_id ownership + branch fence (verified OrderService:1428-1444). However the route is only behind `auth:sanctum` — no role check. Anyone logged in with sanctum can hit /api/frontend/delivery-boy-order/show/{order} ; the service throws 403 if not theirs. Defense-in-depth would add a `role:Delivery Boy` route guard.
findings.evidence: Route 1205: middleware(['auth:sanctum']) — no role guard. Service-level ownership check is the only fence.
findings.recommendation: V1.0.2 backlog: add `role:Delivery Boy,sanctum` to the prefix group. Mark deferred-heal.

findings.title: Missing rate-limit on driver status change endpoint
findings.description: POST /api/frontend/delivery-boy-order/change-status/{order} has no per-IP throttle or idempotency key. A misbehaving driver client (or replayed token) could flap the order through transitions rapidly. AuditLogService chain has Cache::lock 5s per row but ValidStatusTransition rejects back-jumps, so the cap is logical, not throughput.
findings.evidence: Route 1209: no throttle key. Only auth:sanctum.
findings.recommendation: V1.0.2 backlog: add throttle:60,1 (60 req/min). Mark deferred-heal. Not gating V1.

findings.title: selectDeliveryBoy: BranchScope bypass is intentional + properly fenced
findings.description: OrderService::selectDeliveryBoy line 2125-2138 uses `withoutGlobalScope(BranchScope::class)` to find the target driver, then verifies `$target->branch_id === $order->branch_id` (line 2136). This is the ONLY way Admin (branch_id=0) can resolve a target driver in another branch. The branch-fence check directly after is the security primitive. Audit-log row at line 2151-2166 records actor + path. No bypass — verified.
findings.reproduction: Read OrderService.php line 2095-2181 (deep verification of selectDeliveryBoy guards).
findings.evidence: Line 2127-2130 (withoutGlobalScope+role+id), line 2132 (target null), line 2136 (branch-fence), line 2151 (audit). All four guards present.
findings.recommendation: No heal. Confirmed defense-in-depth correct. NF525 audit chain extended properly (`order.delivery_boy_assigned`).

findings.title: No idempotency key on status mutation endpoint
findings.description: POST /api/frontend/delivery-boy-order/change-status/{order} accepts no X-Idempotency-Key header. While OrderService:1540 has an idempotent early-return (if $locked->status === $newStatus), a fast double-tap on a flaky 3G link can race past the early-return between two distinct status values. Driver UX issue more than security, but classify as P2 defensive.
findings.recommendation: V1.0.2 backlog: add `idempotency` middleware to driver status endpoint. Deferred-heal.

summary: 1 P1 heal target (address controller permission split — pure RBAC consistency), 3 P2 deferred-heal (frontend role guard, throttle, idempotency), 1 P0-avoided confirmation (selectDeliveryBoy fence properly defended).
